newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two bombs wound 18 in Algeria - newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Two bombs wound 18 in Algeria - newspapers.

text.p: Two bomb explosions have wounded 18 people, two of them seriously, in northeastern Algeria, Algerian newspapers said on Monday.

It was the first report of the attacks outside Algiers where security forces on Sunday said a bomb in a city cafe had wounded 20 people. Hospital and other sources said the cafe blast wounded 53 and the newspaper l'Authentique said on Monday that one of these had since died in hospital.

One of the bombs outside the capital, planted on a road in the coastal region of Kolea, 40 km (25 miles) west of Algiers, went off on Sunday hitting a vehicle carrying workers, said El Watan newspaper.
The blast wounded 10 people, including two seriously, it said.

Eight villagers were wounded on Saturday when a bomb exploded under the truck in which they were travelling in Zinedine village, in Ain Defla province, 120 km (75 miles) southwest of Algiers, said Liberte newspaper.
It was in Ain Defla province that Moslem fundamentalists killed 28 people in the early hours of Sunday in Dhamnia community, Algerian security forces reported.
The overnight raid was the fifth such mass killing this month in which the authorities say a total of 82 people have died, many with their throats slit.

Sunday's bomb in the capital exploded inside a cafe in the working class suburb of el Harrach. It was the fourth blast in the Algerian capital within one week in which 19 people were reported to have been killed and 210 hurt.

About 60,000 people have been killed since violence erupted in the North African country after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which the Moslem fundamentalist Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken an overwhelming first-round lead.
